proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(A_0=A(\eta)\), \(W=V\setminus A_0\), and \(E_0=E(G_0(\eta))\).  Membership of \(\eta\) in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), by \(\mathrm{def:compatibility\mbox{-}fiber}\), implies membership in \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\).  Thus the basal graph is acyclic by \(\mathrm{ass:basal\mbox{-}dag}\), selection vertices are childless by \(\mathrm{ass:selection\mbox{-}structure}\), and all of their parents are observed by \(\mathrm{ass:selection\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}domain}\).

First observe that no basal edge points from \(W\) into \(A_0\).  Indeed, if \(w\to a\), where \(w\in W\) and \(a\in A_0\), then the definition of \(A_0\) supplies a directed path from \(a\) to a parent of a selection vertex; concatenation would put \(w\) in \(A_0\), a contradiction.  Consequently a directed cycle in the observed part of \(\widetilde G_0\) cannot cross from \(W\) into \(A_0\).  A cycle contained in \(W\) would already be a cycle of \(G_0(\eta)\), and a cycle contained in \(A_0\) would be a cycle of \(B\).  Neither exists.  The added selection vertices in \(\mathrm{def:basal\mbox{-}replacement}\) are childless, so they cannot lie on a directed cycle.  Hence \(\widetilde G_0\) is acyclic.

Denote the replacement selection family by \(\widetilde S\).  The word ``add'' in \(\mathrm{def:basal\mbox{-}replacement}\) designates fresh childless vertices; their number is finite because \(A_0\) and \(H[A_0]\) are finite.  Every \(a\in A_0\) directly parents its added singleton selection vertex, whence
\[
A_0\subseteq
\operatorname{An}_{\widetilde G_0}
   (\operatorname{pa}_{\widetilde G_0}(\widetilde S))\cap V.
\]
Conversely, every parent of an old or added selection vertex belongs to \(A_0\), and the absence of an edge from \(W\) into \(A_0\) persists after replacement.  No element of \(W\) can therefore reach such a parent.  This proves
\[
\operatorname{An}_{\widetilde G_0}
   (\operatorname{pa}_{\widetilde G_0}(\widetilde S))\cap V=A_0.
\tag{1}
\]

We next identify the observational skeleton using \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\).  A pair not contained in \(A_0\) has exactly the same basal edge and the same old selection-generating structure as before; no added selection vertex has a parent in \(W\).  For \(x,y\in A_0\), every edge \(xy\in H[A_0]\) is generated by the added pair-parent selection vertex.  Conversely, if \(xy\notin H[A_0]\), then \(xy\notin E(B)\), no added selection vertex has both \(x,y\) as parents, and the no-new-unshielded-collider hypothesis prevents \(B\) from creating a common observed child ancestral to selection with nonadjacent parents \(x,y\).  The retained part of the old graph could only reproduce an adjacency already in \(H\).  Thus
\[
\operatorname{skel}(M_0(\widetilde G_0))=H.
\tag{2}
\]
All endpoints inside \(A_0\) are tails by (1) and the observational endpoint clause of the cited interface.  Any observational adjacency incident to \(W\) must be a retained basal edge: a selection-generating common child would make its endpoint in \(W\) ancestral to selection.  Such an edge has its old basal orientation.  Hence the whole observational endpoint pattern, and therefore its unshielded colliders, is unchanged.

Fix \(k\in[K]\), and set
\[
R_k=Z_k\cap A_0.
\]
The indicator formula in the cited interface and the inclusion \(T_k(\eta)\subseteq F_k(\eta)\) give
\[
R_k=F_k(\eta)\cap A_0.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(x\to y\in B\) and \(x\in R_k\), then \(k\in\sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\), hence \(y\in R_k\).  Thus \(R_k\) is descendant closed in \(B\).  Because \(B\) is a finite DAG, every element of \(R_k\) descends from an ancestry-minimal element of \(R_k\).  No retained target in \(W\) can reach \(A_0\), by the no-entry observation above.  The generator clause in \(\mathrm{def:basal\mbox{-}replacement}\) therefore yields
\[
\operatorname{de}_{\widetilde G_0}(\widetilde T_k)\cap A_0=R_k.
\tag{4}
\]

The affected set is also unchanged on \(W\).  For an old target-to-\(w\) path with \(w\in W\), either its target is in \(W\), in which case the path never enters \(A_0\) and is retained, or the path has a last vertex \(r\in A_0\), where \(r\in R_k\), followed only by retained edges.  Equation (4) supplies a replacement target-to-\(r\) prefix, proving the old-to-new inclusion.  Conversely, a new target-to-\(w\) path either starts at a retained target in \(W\), or leaves \(A_0\) for the last time at some \(r\in R_k\).  By (3), an old target reaches \(r\), and the suffix after \(r\) is retained, proving the new-to-old inclusion.  Hence
\[
\operatorname{de}_{\widetilde G_0}(\widetilde T_k)\cap V=F_k(\eta).
\tag{5}
\]
On \(W\), indicator neighbors are exactly retained direct targets; on \(A_0\), (4) and the indicator formula give exactly \(R_k\).  Therefore
\[
\widetilde T_k\cup
\Bigl(\bigl(\operatorname{de}_{\widetilde G_0}(\widetilde T_k)\cap V\bigr)
          \setminus\widetilde T_k\Bigr)\cap A_0
=Z_k,
\tag{6}
\]
where the first term and the parenthesized second term are respectively the direct-target and indirectly affected selected contributions.

By the regime-adjacency clause of the cited interface, a regime skeleton is a function only of \(H\), \(A_0\), and the affected selected set \(R_k\).  Equations (1)--(5) therefore imply equality of the regime-\(k\) skeletons, including all indicator adjacencies by (6).

It remains to compare unshielded colliders.  Every regime adjacency incident to \(W\) is a retained observational directed edge, because an intervention-created adjacency has both endpoints in \(A_0\); hence its endpoint marks are unchanged.  Consider a possible collider center \(c\in A_0\).  An incident edge from \(c\) to \(W\) has a tail at \(c\), so it cannot contribute an arrowhead at that center.  If \(c\notin R_k\), the endpoint rule in the cited interface gives a tail at \(c\) on every selected--selected incident edge.  If \(c\in R_k\) and two observed vertices \(a,b\in A_0\) are regime neighbors of \(c\), concatenate their witnessing \(H[A_0]\)-paths to \(c\).  Since \(c\) and every internal vertex are in \(R_k\), deleting loops gives an admissible path from \(a\) to \(b\); thus \(a,b\) are adjacent and the triple is shielded.  Finally, if one neighbor is \(\zeta_k\), then \(c\in R_k\).  An observed neighbor \(a\in R_k\) is adjacent to \(\zeta_k\), so the triple is shielded, whereas for \(a\notin R_k\) the cited endpoint rule fixes \(a\to c\leftarrow\zeta_k\).  This last unshielded-collider condition depends only on the already preserved skeleton and \(R_k\).  At \(\zeta_k\) all incident marks are tails.  These cases exhaust all centers and prove equality of every unshielded-collider family on \(U_k\).

Since \(k\) was arbitrary, (1), (2), (6), and the collider argument establish every assertion of the lemma.  No division, support limit, rank condition, or probability-kernel assertion is used. \(\square\)

Work against the corrected construction in \(\mathrm{def:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}specification}\), in which the selection edge is \(1\to s\).  Take all variables binary.  Let \(X_1\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and, conditionally on \(X_1\), set
\[
\Pr(X_2=X_1\mid X_1)=\frac34,
\qquad
\Pr(X_2\ne X_1\mid X_1)=\frac14.
\tag{1}
\]
For the selection vertex use the strictly positive kernel
\[
\Pr(S_s^*=1\mid X_1=x_1)=\frac12
\quad\text{for both }x_1\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Finally take \(X_3\) independent of the first component, with
\[
\Pr(X_3=1\mid \text{regime }0)=\frac14,
\qquad
\Pr(X_3=1\mid \text{regime }1)=\frac34.
\tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(3) factorize over the graph in \(\mathrm{def:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}specification}\); the only kernel changed in regime \(1\) is that of the direct target \(3\).  The noises can be chosen independent, so causal sufficiency holds, and (2) gives \(\Pr(S^*=1)=1/2>0\).  The graph is acyclic, its selection vertex is childless, and its only selection parent is observed.  Thus every graphical, factorization, positivity, pre-treatment, and soft-intervention condition in \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\) holds.

Conditioning on \(S_s^*=1\) does not alter the law of \((X_1,X_2,X_3)\).  Under the pooled law,
\[
P_{\eta^\dagger,1}^{\mathrm{pool}}(x_1,x_2,x_3,z)
=P_{12}(x_1,x_2)\,
  \frac12 P_{3,z}(x_3),
\tag{4}
\]
where \(P_{12}\) is the table in (1), \(P_{3,0}(1)=1/4\), and \(P_{3,1}(1)=3/4\).  The two factors in (4) are independent components.  Each of the two binary \(2\)-by-\(2\) tables on \((X_1,X_2)\) and \((\zeta_1,X_3)\) has nonzero determinant: for the first, \(P(X_1=X_2)=3/4\ne1/2\), and for the second the two conditional success probabilities in (3) differ.  Consequently neither edge's endpoints become independent after conditioning on variables in the other component, while every cross-component conditional independence holds by the product in (4).  This is exactly faithfulness to the disjoint union of the single edges supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\).  Hence \(\eta^\dagger\in\mathfrak M_{3,1}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\).

The only parent of selection is \(1\), so
\[
A(\eta^\dagger)
=\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta^\dagger)}(\{1\})\cap V
=\{1\}.
\tag{5}
\]
The target \(3\) has no observed descendants other than itself, so the indicator-neighbor formula gives
\[
Z_1=T_1\cup
  \bigl((F_1\setminus T_1)\cap A(\eta^\dagger)\bigr)
=\{3\}.
\tag{6}
\]
In the observational MAG, the endpoint at \(1\) is a tail because \(1\in A(\eta^\dagger)\), while the endpoint at \(2\) is an arrowhead because \(2\notin A(\eta^\dagger)\) and \(2\notin\operatorname{An}_{G_0}(1)\).  Thus the observational edge is \(1\to2\), and it is retained in the regime MAG by the retained-directed-edge clause of the cited interface.  Its endpoint at \(2\) is therefore an arrowhead although \(2\notin Z_1\) by (6).  This explicit member proves that target membership cannot characterize arrowheads on retained adjacencies. \(\square\)

Let \(uv\) be absent from \(H\) and present in the regime-\(k\) skeleton.  The regime-adjacency equivalence in \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\) rules out its observational-adjacency alternative.  It therefore supplies an \(H\)-path from \(u\) to \(v\) whose endpoints and internal vertices are all in \(A(\eta)\), with every internal vertex affected in regime \(k\).  In particular,
\[
u\in A(\eta),\qquad v\in A(\eta).
\]
The source lemma is graphical, so no positivity, rank, conditioning denominator, or limiting argument enters this implication. \(\square\)

For \(r\ge0\), let \(C^{(r)}=C^{(r)}(\mathcal O)\) be the recursion in \(\mathrm{def:observable\mbox{-}selectedness\mbox{-}closure}\).  We prove by induction that
\[
C^{(r)}\subseteq A(\eta).
\tag{1}
\]
For \(r=0\), each vertex in \(C^{(0)}\) is an endpoint of an intervention-created adjacency.  Equation (1) follows from \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}visible\mbox{-}selectedness}\).

Assume (1) at stage \(r\), and suppose that \(x\) is newly adjoined because \(i-x-j\) is an observational unshielded noncollider with nonadjacent endpoints \(i,j\in C^{(r)}\).  The induction hypothesis gives \(i,j\in A(\eta)\).  Suppose for contradiction that \(x\notin A(\eta)\).  By the observational-adjacency clause of \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\), the adjacency \(ix\) cannot be generated by a common child ancestral to selection, since then \(x\) itself would be ancestral to selection.  It is therefore a basal edge.  It cannot be oriented \(x\to i\), because \(i\in A(\eta)\) would then imply \(x\in A(\eta)\).  Hence it is \(i\to x\).  The same reasoning gives \(j\to x\).  Because \(i\) and \(j\) are nonadjacent, the observational triple is the unshielded collider
\[
i\to x\leftarrow j,
\]
contrary to its defining noncollider status.  Thus \(x\in A(\eta)\), completing the induction.

The recursion stops after at most \(|V|\) strict vertex additions, and its definition takes the union through stage \(|V|\).  Therefore
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)
=\bigcup_{r=0}^{|V|}C^{(r)}(\mathcal O)
\subseteq A(\eta).
\]
All inputs to the recursion are components of \(\mathcal O\), so this is an observable sound certificate and does not query a compatible model. \(\square\)

For each of the \(K+1\) reported regimes there are at most \(\binom D2\) observed--observed adjacencies and two endpoints per adjacency.  Hence the number of reported endpoint positions is at most
\[
N_{\mathrm{end}}
\le 2(K+1)\binom D2
=(K+1)D(D-1)
\le 2(K+1)D(D-1).
\tag{1}
\]
By hypothesis, a strict conclusion changes a circle to a definite mark, and no rule changes a definite mark.  Charge each strict update to the endpoint changed.  Each endpoint is charged at most once, so (1) proves the asserted update bound.

Because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is fixed and finite, there are constants \(q,r,c\), independent of \(D\) and \(K\), such that a rule has at most \(q\) observed-vertex placeholders and \(r\) regime placeholders and there are at most \(c\) rule schemata.  A complete scan has at most
\[
cD^q(K+1)^r
\tag{2}
\]
instances.  By the premise-decider hypothesis, the cost of each instance is bounded by a polynomial in \(D\), \(K\), and the encoding length of \(\mathcal O\).  After each strict update perform another complete scan, and stop after the first scan with no update.  Equations (1) and (2) bound the number of scans and the work per scan by polynomials; thus the resulting saturation algorithm is polynomial.

By \(\mathrm{def:monotone\mbox{-}closure}\), the skeletons and unshielded-collider families on every \(U_k\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving input facts, are immutable during these scans.  The algorithm therefore computes exactly the least monotone fixed point \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\).  If the additional equality
\[
\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)
\]
holds, substitution identifies the computed fixed point with the canonical SI-PAG of \(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}si\mbox{-}pag}\).  The algorithm has used only rule matching and has never enumerated \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\). \(\square\)

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), put \(A=A(\eta)\), \(F_k=\operatorname{de}_{G_0(\eta)}(T_k(\eta))\cap V\), and let \(H\) be the observational skeleton.  In the causally sufficient childless-selection pre-treatment twin construction, Dai et al.'s Lemmas 3--6 give the following facts.  Observational adjacency is generated by a basal observed edge or by an observed common child that is ancestral to selection.  An observed pair is adjacent in regime \(k\) exactly when it is observationally adjacent or its endpoints are joined in \(H[A]\) by a path whose internal vertices belong to \(F_k\cap A\).  The indicator-neighbor set is
\[
\operatorname{adj}_{M_k(\eta)}(\zeta_k)\cap V
=T_k(\eta)\cup\bigl((F_k\setminus T_k(\eta))\cap A\bigr).
\]
Every indicator edge is oriented out of \(\zeta_k\).  An observed directed edge of the observational MAG is retained in the regime MAG.  For any other regime adjacency \(xy\), its marks are determined as follows: two unaffected endpoints give \(x\mathbin{-}y\); if \(y\) is affected and either \(x\) is unaffected or \(x\in\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta)}(y)\), the edge is \(x\to y\); the symmetric condition gives \(y\to x\); and two affected endpoints with neither ancestral to the other give \(x\leftrightarrow y\).  In particular, observational endpoints inside \(A\) are tails, and an observational adjacency meeting \(V\setminus A\) is a basal directed edge with its basal orientation.

source.locator: Lemmas 3--6, main text pp. 6--7 and proofs in Appendix B

attestation.note: The displayed interface was checked clause by clause against Lemmas 3--6 in the source-of-record PDF and against the main-attested author-source transcription preserved in the immutable prior-run core.

added_lemmas.justification: This cited leaf supplies exactly the published twin-MAG adjacency, indicator-neighbor, and endpoint formulas used by the new replacement arguments.
added_lemmas.gap: The cited result does not contain the replacement construction or any cross-regime faithful-kernel realization.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is used by the graphical replacement, retained-edge, and observable selectedness proofs.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: There exists a finite-alphabet model \(\eta^\dagger\in\mathfrak M_{3,1}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) whose graph and target data equal \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\). For every such faithful model, \(A(\eta^\dagger)=\{1\}\), \(Z_1=\{3\}\), and Dai et al.'s retained-edge result gives \(1\to2\) in \(M_1(\eta^\dagger)\). Consequently, the endpoint at vertex \(2\) on that retained adjacency is an arrowhead although \(2\notin Z_1\). The corrected endpoint frontier therefore makes its arrowhead equivalence only for intervention-created adjacencies \(uv\notin H\); it makes no target-membership equivalence for retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: With the frozen edge \(2\to s\), the definition gives \(A=\{1,2\}\), so the observational and unaffected regime edge is \(1\mathbin{-}2\), not \(1\to2\). Moving the selection-parent edge to \(1\to s\) makes \(A=\{1\}\) and yields the intended retained arrowhead at the nonselected endpoint \(2\). The proposed claim records that smaller selected set and no longer asserts the false equality.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Set \(D=3\), \(K=1\), \(V=\{1,2,3\}\), and \(S=\{s\}\). Define \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\) by the basal selected DAG \(E(G_0)=\{1\to2,1\to s\}\), with vertex \(3\) isolated in the basal DAG, and the direct soft-intervention target \(T_1=\{3\}\). No other basal edge or direct target is present.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The frozen construction \(1\to2\to s\) puts both endpoints in \(A\), so Dai et al.'s endpoint formula makes the unaffected retained edge undirected and cannot witness an arrowhead outside \(Z_1\). Replacing \(2\to s\) by \(1\to s\) preserves the three-variable retained-edge design while making endpoint \(2\) nonselected, which is exactly the advertised sanity witness.

proposed.statement: Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\). If \(B\) is acyclic, every edge of \(B\) lies in \(H[A(\eta)]\), \(B\) creates no unshielded collider whose endpoints are nonadjacent in \(H\), and every \(x\to y\in B\) satisfies \(\sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\), then the basal DAG \(\widetilde G_0\) in \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{An}_{\widetilde G_0}(\operatorname{pa}_{\widetilde G_0}(S))\cap V=A(\eta)\). For every \(k=0,\ldots,K\), the twin graph determined by \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) has a latent-projection MAG on \(U_k\) with exactly the adjacency and unshielded-collider signature of \(M_k(\eta)\), including every adjacency and every unshielded collider involving \(\zeta_k\). For \(k\in[K]\), its target and descendant data realize \(Z_k=\widetilde T_k\cup((\operatorname{de}_{\widetilde G_0}(\widetilde T_k)\cap V\setminus\widetilde T_k)\cap A(\eta))\), with the two terms representing direct targets and indirectly affected ancestrally selected vertices separately.
proposed.justification: This lemma isolates the graph-theoretic obligation: the replacement specification preserves the full oracle signature before any probability law is chosen.
proposed.gap: Dai et al., Lemmas 4--6 on pp. 6--7, give the intervention-created adjacency, indicator-neighbor, and endpoint semantics used here, but do not give a synchronized common-basal graph replacement preserving every indicator-involving signature constraint.
proposed.consumer: It supplies the graphical half of each opposing selected-endpoint witness used by the complete calculus.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses Dai et al.'s published twin-MAG formulas, now materialized as the cited Dai twin-MAG interface lemma.

proposed.statement: There exists a finite-alphabet model \(\eta^\dagger\in\mathfrak M_{3,1}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) whose graph and target data equal \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\). For every such faithful model, \(A(\eta^\dagger)=\{1\}\), \(Z_1=\{3\}\), and Dai et al.'s retained-edge result gives \(1\to2\) in \(M_1(\eta^\dagger)\). Consequently, the endpoint at vertex \(2\) on that retained adjacency is an arrowhead although \(2\notin Z_1\). The corrected endpoint frontier therefore makes its arrowhead equivalence only for intervention-created adjacencies \(uv\notin H\); it makes no target-membership equivalence for retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\).
proposed.justification: The explicit three-variable reduction separates retained basal orientation from the target-driven orientation mechanism and removes the failed normalization.
proposed.gap: Dai et al., Lemma 6 on p. 7, supplies retained-edge semantics; target membership controls intervention-created adjacencies through a distinct mechanism and cannot characterize retained-edge arrowheads.
proposed.consumer: It gives an executable unit check for any implementation of the fixed-selected-set endpoint frontier.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The retained-edge orientation is an explicit use of the cited Dai twin-MAG endpoint formula.

proposed.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), with \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O(\eta)\) formed from the faithful pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), if \(uv\) is absent from the observational skeleton \(H\) and present in an observed intervention-regime skeleton, then \(u,v\in A(\eta)\).
proposed.justification: Dai et al.'s Lemma 4 supplies the initial visible-selectedness certificate used by the rule handle.
proposed.gap: Dai et al., Lemma 4 on p. 6, is the published source of this intervention-created-adjacency certificate; the closure of partially certified selection membership is not part of that lemma.
proposed.consumer: It initializes cross-regime selectedness without analyst-supplied labels.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof is a direct specialization of Dai et al.'s intervention-created-adjacency characterization and must declare that cited leaf.

proposed.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), with \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O(\eta)\) formed from the faithful pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), the entirely observable closure satisfies \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\subseteq A(\eta)\). The seed inclusion is Dai et al.'s intervention-created-adjacency certificate. At each recursive step, if \(i,j\in\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\) are the nonadjacent endpoints of an observational unshielded noncollider \(i-x-j\), then \(x\in A(\eta)\), so adjoining \(x\) preserves the inclusion.
proposed.justification: This theorem turns the noncollider closure into an observable sound certificate set that can legally appear in rule premises.
proposed.gap: Dai et al., Lemma 4 on p. 6, provides the cross-regime seed but does not state this noncollider closure; Wang, Du, and Zhou instead take singleton background knowledge as supplied.
proposed.consumer: It supplies the model-free selectedness predicate used by the local calculus while reserving \(A(\eta)\) for completeness witnesses.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The induction step uses the published observational adjacency and endpoint clauses in addition to the seed lemma.

proposed.statement: Fix \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\). If every rule premise and path predicate is decidable uniformly in time polynomial in \(D\), \(K\), and the encoding length of \(\mathcal O\), and every conclusion changes a reported circle endpoint once to a tail or arrowhead, then saturation makes at most \(2(K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates and computes \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) in polynomial time. The observational skeleton and unshielded colliders on \(U_0=V\), together with the complete skeletons and unshielded-collider families of the faithful pooled selected-law signatures on \(U_k\), \(k\in[K]\), including all indicator adjacencies and indicator-involving unshielded colliders, remain immutable inputs. If additionally \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\), this polynomial output is the canonical SI-PAG and no enumeration of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) is required.
proposed.justification: This conditional closure-accounting corollary records the computational consequence of a fixed finite grammar and one-way endpoint updates.
proposed.gap: The proposition is not an independent novelty claim; its substantive identification content comes entirely from the complete-calculus theorem.
proposed.consumer: An implementation can audit rule-predicate complexity before using complete saturation on a perturbation panel.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proposition is conditional on closure equality and its proof does not use the unresolved complete-calculus theorem; removing that dependency prevents a proved bookkeeping result from depending on an open theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that the shared finite-alphabet parameter space for every admissible replacement contains kernels whose selected pooled laws are simultaneously faithful to all \(M_k\).
open_obligations.obstruction: Faithfulness is imposed on members already in \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), but no frozen assumption or cited theorem makes an arbitrary replacement specification a member. Ordinary generic faithfulness for one unconstrained DAG does not cover the common baseline-kernel equalities, conditioning on \(S^*=\mathbf 1\), and all pooled indicator laws at once.
open_obligations.attempted: Parameterize all positive conditional-probability tables and clear the selection denominators in each conditional-independence determinant. This reduces simultaneous unfaithfulness to a finite union of algebraic zero sets, but closure still requires a nonvanishing witness for every \(m\)-connected query on the shared-parameter subspace. That witness was not derived from the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.partial_result: For any fixed replacement specification, strictly positive finite conditional-probability tables can be chosen to factor over \(\widetilde G_0\), the same baseline table can be reused at every non-target vertex, and every selection kernel can be made strictly positive; these choices give Markov factorization, non-target kernel stability, and \(\Pr(S^*=\mathbf 1)>0\).  The graphical replacement lemma already proves the desired projected skeletons and unshielded colliders.  What remains unproved is that the shared-parameter space contains a point at which, simultaneously for every \(k\), conditioning on \(S^*=\mathbf 1\) and pooling the two arms with \(\zeta_k\) introduce no conditional independence beyond the \(m\)-separations of \(M_k(\widetilde\eta)\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Turn the proved graphical replacement specification into a fully specified member of \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\cap\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The graphical proof fixes the projected signatures, but membership in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) additionally requires the unresolved jointly faithful kernel family in \(\mathrm{lem:simultaneous\mbox{-}faithful\mbox{-}realization}\).
open_obligations.attempted: Combined the graphical preservation conclusion with arbitrary strictly positive stable kernels. This establishes factorization, stability, and positive selection but not the reverse, faithfulness direction of every pooled-law conditional-independence equivalence.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved graphical replacement lemma constructs, for every admissible \(B\), one acyclic replacement specification with the same \(A(\eta)\), every regime skeleton, every unshielded collider, and every indicator neighborhood.  Conditional on the still-unproved simultaneous-faithful-realization assertion, selecting its model \(\widetilde\eta\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) and applying \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}signature}\) gives \(\mathcal O(\widetilde\eta)=\mathcal O\) and hence the entire conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\).  Thus the sole remaining implication is from the graphical replacement specification to a jointly faithful shared-kernel member of \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Promote the empty-subgraph and signature-monotone-path graphical witnesses to whole-family models in the fixed-\(A\) compatibility fiber.
open_obligations.obstruction: The endpoint necessity and both replacement graphs follow from the Dai formulas, but the theorem quantifies over fully specified faithful models. That last quantifier cannot be discharged while simultaneous faithful realization is open.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the necessity direction and used \(B=\varnothing\) for an arrowhead specification and a simple path in \(L_{A(\eta)}\) for a tail specification. The graphical replacement lemma preserves every full-regime signature; only faithful kernel realization remains.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The fixed-\(A\) necessity is graphical.  For an intervention-created adjacency \(uv\) with \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), the Dai endpoint formula gives
\[
\mu(u)=\mathtt{arrow}\Longrightarrow u\in Z_k,
\qquad
\mu(u)=\mathtt{tail}\Longrightarrow
\bigl(u\notin Z_k\bigr)\ \text{or}\ u\in\operatorname{An}_{G_0}(v).
\]
If \(u\in\operatorname{An}_{G_0}(v)\), an ancestral path cannot leave and re-enter the ancestor-closed set \(A(\eta)\); every path edge lies in \(H[A(\eta)]\), and descendant closure of every \(Z_\ell\cap A(\eta)\) gives \(\sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\) along the path.  Hence \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\).  Conversely, the empty choice of \(B\) gives the graphical arrowhead witness when \(u\in Z_k\), and a simple \(L_{A(\eta)}\)-path from \(u\) to \(v\), used as \(B\), gives the graphical tail witness.  Such a path is acyclic and has no vertex with two incoming path edges.  The proved graphical replacement lemma preserves all regime signatures for both specifications.  Promoting these two graphical specifications to members of \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\) is exactly the unresolved simultaneous-faithful-realization step.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct an explicit fixed finite observable rule list and prove that every residual circle has two common-basal whole-family extensions without guessing \(A\) or invoking global feasibility.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen handle is a development recipe, not a rule list. The proved closure only certifies a subset of every feasible \(A\); it gives no local criterion that chooses compatible unknown selection membership and one exterior DAG completion while preserving all regime fill edges and indicator colliders. The presolve draft explicitly identifies this coupled lift as unresolved.
open_obligations.attempted: Used intervention-created edges as observable selectedness seeds, proved the noncollider closure sound, and reduced fixed-\(A\) selected endpoints to signature-monotone reachability. These steps do not synchronize unknown \(A\), the exterior completion, and all regimes, and no permitted finite rule schema was found that does so.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved certificate result gives \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\subseteq A(\eta)\) for every compatible \(\eta\), so membership in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}\) is a sound observable rule premise.  Conditional on a fixed compatible \(A\), the empty selected subgraph and a simple signature-monotone path supply the two graphical endpoint specifications described in the fixed-\(A\) partial result.  These facts do not select a compatible \(A\), do not complete the exterior DAG, and do not provide a fixed local rule list whose residual circles certify that both choices extend simultaneously across every regime.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish existence, soundness, and mark completeness of one \(D,K\)-independent finite local SI rule calculus.
open_obligations.obstruction: The theorem depends on the unresolved selection-lifting OEQ, and the core supplies neither an explicit \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) nor opposing witnesses across unknown selected sets and common exterior completions. Defining the canonical invariant does not prove that the restricted grammar computes it.
open_obligations.attempted: Proved the graphical fixed-set replacement mechanism, observable selectedness certificates, a retained-edge boundary, and conditional polynomial saturation. The missing local extension theorem cannot be replaced by the excluded global basal-DAG enumerator or by assuming a feasible \(A\).
open_obligations.partial_result: If the open selection-lifting question had a positive resolution with a finite sound list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\), its extension property would show that every endpoint left circular by saturation has both marks among models in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\).  Soundness would give the reverse inclusion of definite marks.  Endpoint by endpoint, \(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}si\mbox{-}pag}\) would then yield \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\).  The proved polynomial-saturation proposition would supply the conditional computation bound.  No such rule list or unknown-selection extension proof is present in the frozen core, so this conditional reduction does not prove the existential theorem.
